- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days.
- If true price drops sharply after forecast peak, model fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust downward by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags 1–3 days behind true trend; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is positive, or 1–2% downward if negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- When true price is below 65% of historical mean, model often underestimates; add 3–5% upward bias for next 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
